open_points.subject: R0-89 versus the one-home rule
open_points.text: R0-80 says that customer personal data is "held only by Registry" and admits only issued documents and Client Portal's offline projection, while R0-89 requires an export, customer names and tax-id answers to be kept in the owner's Bitwarden.
open_points.question: Is the vault copy a new temporary exception to R0-80's one-home rule, or is some part of the migration material required to omit personal data?
options: Add the vault material as a governed temporary exception
Remove personal values from the retained migration material
Replace the retained material with another recovery mechanism
open_points.default_guess: Treat the vault material as a temporary governed exception lasting until a checked backup holds the import.

open_points.subject: Recreation of post-backup records
open_points.text: "Projects, Customers, rooms and pointers first made after the backup are made again by the ordinary actions" does not name where the values required by those actions come from.
open_points.question: What retained source supplies each lost project's name, customer link and object data, each Customer's personal data, room names, and pointer type, reference and digest?
options: The affected consumer and producer services
The owner's memory and surviving documents
No guaranteed recreation of unreconstructable records
open_points.default_guess: Use an owner-held recovery journal, and leave an unreconstructable record absent with the loss recorded in governance.

open_points.subject: Recreation of post-backup records
open_points.text: "Projects, Customers, rooms and pointers first made after the backup are made again by the ordinary actions" is passive, although rooms and pointers have both owner and agent-authority actions.
open_points.question: Who is responsible for recreating each kind of lost record, especially rooms and artifact pointers: the owner, an agent through Kernel, or the original writer?
options: The original permitted actor recreates each record
The owner recreates identity records and an agent recreates links
open_points.default_guess: The owner recreates all records through the owner interface.

open_points.subject: Old-to-new identity correspondence
open_points.text: "Registry keeps no correspondence between them and the lost ones, which the owner's record and the consumers hold" does not identify the owner's record or define how the correspondence is created, stored, protected, updated or retired.
open_points.question: What record holds each lost-to-recreated project, Customer, room and pointer identity mapping, who writes it, and for how long must it remain available?
options: Create a separate owner-held recovery mapping
Keep mappings only in each affected consumer
open_points.default_guess: Keep a separate owner-held recovery mapping in the vault until every affected consumer has completed relinking and the recovery is backed up.

open_points.subject: Consumer relinking after recovery
open_points.text: R0-89 says that mappings are "for the owner's record and the consumers alike" and that consumers "hold" correspondence, but names no delivery, acknowledgement or failure behavior for those consumers.
open_points.question: How does each affected consumer receive and apply an old-to-new identity mapping, how is completion observed, and what happens when a consumer or mapping is unavailable?
options: Manual relinking with recorded acknowledgement from every affected service
Consumer pull from an owner-provided mapping file
Best-effort relinking with stale references left unresolved
open_points.default_guess: Use manual per-service relinking, record completion, and retain the mapping while any affected service remains unresolved.

open_points.subject: Recovery timestamps on repeated marks
open_points.text: "every other mark carries the instant of its repetition" does not identify which marks it covers or whether the instant belongs to the domain record, the audit entry, or both.
open_points.question: Which repeated actions create a timestamped mark, where is that timestamp stored, and is it observable through existing reads?
options: Only the new audit entry carries the repetition instant
Restriction, erasure and anonymisation marks gain stored timestamps
Both the domain mark and audit entry carry it
open_points.default_guess: Only the new audit entry carries the repetition instant unless an existing model already defines a timestamp for that mark.
